contentHtml:
In the competitive and rapidly evolving labor market of the Kingdom, the end of service benefits in Saudi Arabia (often referred to as “gratuity”) represent a fundamental right for every employee and a significant financial obligation for every employer. Under the framework of Saudi Vision 2030, the rules governing these payments have become more transparent, digitalized, and strictly enforced to ensure market fairness.

At Connect Resources, we specialize in navigating the complexities of Saudi Labor Law. Whether you are an HR professional managing a large workforce or an expatriate planning your next career move, understanding the latest end of service benefit rules in Saudi Arabia is crucial for financial compliance and peace of mind.

1. What are End of Service Benefits (EOSB)?

The End of Service Benefit (EOSB) is a mandatory lump-sum payment that an employer must pay to a worker upon the termination of the employment contract. Governed primarily by Articles 84 and 85 of the Saudi Labor Law, this benefit serves as a “thank you” for the years of service and a financial cushion for the transition period.

Core Eligibility in 2026:

  • Who: All private-sector employees (Saudi and Expatriates) under a valid labor contract.

  • When: Payable upon contract expiry, resignation, termination, retirement, or death.

  • Threshold: Generally requires a minimum of two consecutive years of service to qualify for any payment upon resignation.

2. The Standard Calculation Formula (Article 84)

The end of service benefits calculator in saudi arabia follows a tiered accrual system based on the “Actual Wage” (Basic salary plus fixed allowances like housing and transport).

The Formula Breakdown:

  • First 5 Years of Service: Half a month’s wage for each year.

  • Years Beyond 5: One full month’s wage for each subsequent year.

Calculation Example:

If an employee earns SAR 10,000 and works for 8 years:

  • First 5 years: 5 X 0.5 X 10,000 = SAR 25,000

  • Remaining 3 years: 3 X 1.0 X 10,000 = SAR 30,000

  • Total Accrued Benefit: SAR 55,000

3. End of Service Benefit Rules in Saudi Arabia for Resignation

If an employee chooses to resign, Article 85 applies a “reduction tier” to the total accrued benefit. This is one of the most critical end of service benefit rules in Saudi Arabia to understand:

Tenure (Service Period) Resignation Entitlement
Less than 2 Years Zero (0%)
2 to 5 Years One-Third (1/3) of the total
5 to 10 Years Two-Thirds (2/3) of the total
10+ Years Full (100%) entitlement

4. Special Cases: Full Award Entitlement

There are specific scenarios where an employee is entitled to the full (100%) benefit, regardless of the resignation tiers mentioned above:

  1. Force Majeure: If the employee is forced to leave due to circumstances beyond their control.

  2. Female Employee Resignation: * Within 6 months of marriage.

    • Within 3 months of giving birth.

  3. Article 81 Scenarios: If the employee resigns because the employer failed to meet contractual obligations (e.g., non-payment of wages) or committed an act of violence.

5. Digital Compliance: Using the Official Calculator

In 2026, manual calculations are often prone to errors that lead to labor disputes. The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) provides an official end of service benefits calculator in saudi arabia on the Qiwa and MHRSD portals.

Why use the official portal?

  • Real-time Accuracy: It reflects the latest 2026 legislative amendments.

  • Pro-rata Accuracy: It calculates benefits down to the specific number of days worked in the final year.

  • WPS Integration: Payments processed through the Wage Protection System must align with these official calculations.

6. How Connect Resources Saudi Simplifies Your EOSB Management

Managing end of service benefits in Saudi Arabia can be a heavy administrative burden. Connect Resources acts as your strategic partner to ensure 100% compliance:

  • Automated Accruals: We track and calculate EOSB for your outsourced staff every month, so there are no financial surprises at the end of a contract.

  • Qiwa Management: We handle the digital offboarding process, ensuring that the “Reason for Termination” is correctly logged to trigger the right payment tier.

  • Conflict Resolution: Our legal experts mediate between employers and employees to ensure settlements are fair and compliant with the latest end of service benefit rules in Saudi Arabia.

7. Conclusion: Transparency in the 2026 Labor Market

The end of service benefits in Saudi Arabia are a cornerstone of the Kingdom’s “fair work” initiative. By providing a clear and reliable end of service benefits calculator in saudi arabia, the government has made it easier for businesses to attract and retain top talent. For employers, the key to success in 2026 is meticulous record-keeping and a proactive approach to final settlements.

FAQ: End of Service Benefits KSA

Q1: Is the EOSB calculated on the basic salary or total package?

It is calculated on the Actual Wage, which includes the basic salary plus fixed allowances (like housing and transport) as stated in the employment contract.

Q2: Can an employer deny EOSB if the employee is fired?

Only under Article 80 (Gross Misconduct). If the employee is fired for a reason not covered by Article 80, they are still entitled to their full accrued benefits.

Q3: How soon must the EOSB be paid?

If the employer terminates the contract, they must pay within one week. If the employee resigns, the employer has two weeks to settle all dues.
